title: Elephant-cage HF antennas may have aided Sherman's downloads
summary: Jesse Michels tells of Elephant-cage HF antennas may have aided Sherman's downloads, about early 1990s at San Vito dei Normanni Air Station, Italy; Offutt AFB, Nebraska, and frames it as the host. As told, not a fact.
place_text: San Vito dei Normanni Air Station, Italy; Offutt AFB, Nebraska

tellings.quote: antennas. Were these antennas and the signals they received somehow very important for the signals that Dan himself was trying [music] to decode for the NSA?

plain: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, discusses Dan Sherman, a former sergeant who says in his book Above Black that the NSA, the US agency that intercepts signals, hired him to communicate with aliens. Michels wonders whether huge high-frequency radio antenna arrays nicknamed elephant cages, at bases such as San Vito dei Normanni in Italy and Offutt in Nebraska in the early 1990s, and the signals they received, mattered for the messages Sherman was trying to decode, which, if so, would tie his story to real listening equipment.
